name: OscSNS
full_name: Oscillation search at the Spallation Neutron Source
summary: OscSNS was a proposed short-baseline neutrino-oscillation detector at Oak Ridge. It sought to test the LSND anomaly with the pulsed pion- and muon-decay-at-rest neutrino source at the SNS.
physics_targets: Short-baseline sterile-neutrino appearance and disappearance tests
Low-energy neutrino interactions on carbon and electrons
detection_principle: A mineral-oil detector with a small scintillator admixture would identify electron-antineutrino appearance through prompt positrons and delayed neutron capture. Neutrino interactions on carbon and electron scattering provide additional channels; beam timing suppresses cosmic backgrounds.

sites.name: SNS, Oak Ridge National Laboratory
sites.location: Oak Ridge, Tennessee; proposed detector location

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The white paper is a design proposal; no operating OscSNS detector is established. The INFN directory lists OscSNS under expired projects.

collaboration.name: OscSNS Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Baseline
key_parameters.value: Approximately 60 m from the SNS target, in the backward direction

key_parameters.name: Source
key_parameters.value: Pion and muon decay at rest, with the muon-decay spectrum ending near 52.8 MeV

results.summary: Published detector design and projected sensitivity; its simulated contours are not measured exclusion limits.

science_scope: This dossier preserves a named historical proposal. Design parameters and sensitivity estimates are not measured neutrino results; later programmes using the same laboratory or technology are distinct.
